speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with postpartum fever and abdominal tenderness. To help me understand your condition, have you experienced any vaginal discharge or foul-smelling lochia since giving birth?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Puerperal Metritis with possible Urinary Tract Involvement.

Based on your history of a prolonged labor, 11-pound baby delivery, current fever, uterine tenderness, and decreased bowel sounds, the clinical picture strongly suggests an infection of the uterus (puerperal metritis), potentially complicated by a urinary tract issue. I am requesting the following to confirm this: REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) and REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis & Culture. Do you have any specific pain when urinating?
